handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first reading of all 106 annotated verse positions, with manuscript-specific spellings and observed interventions. A different agent subsequently inspected all source verses and every evidence note; see revision record and second-pass ledger.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l represents a verse and physical written line at its canonical poem position. Elegiac couplets and even-line indentation are editorial display grouping. Page breaks follow the photographed left/right physical pages. Facsimile zones reproduce the existing annotation rectangles unchanged; they may include neighbouring ink and exclude marginal annotations.

interpretation.p: First-pass evidence notes are a working queue for an independent agent, not assignments for the human editor. Genuine source uncertainty remains local; consequential unresolved interpretation is distinguished from ordinary observation.

revisionDesc.change: Independent second-agent source review of all 106 verses and every editorial note. A different agent inspected all 106 physical verse positions and all 70 author notes. The reading qui at 6 is corrected to tentative uix, and amore at 60 to in ore. Additional tentative fragments are recovered at 4, 8, 10, 24, 29, 30, 34, 48, and 59; the partial gaps elsewhere remain explicit. Fluminum amores at 101 is now readable as written-out letters. Adire at 97 receives a new local uncertainty note. Heavy image 89 staining and other pale passages are not filled from an edition or another witness. No human approval is implied.
Completed first reading from source images and enlarged crops, with line coverage and evidence notes. Independent second reading not yet performed.

div.note: The decorated initial and tentative mnis arundinibus are visible at the bottom of image 89 left. Opaque staining obscures the right; no additional complete word is independently recoverable.
The physical second verse is present below the initial line. The stain and fading prevent an independent complete-word reading, so the extant-position gap remains.
The opening of image 89 right is under a broad black patch. Pontes and the pale continuation are present; nec te sine remigis ictu remains tentative. The patch does not establish scribal deletion.
The final pale word is compatible with uehat and is now retained under unclear. The stained opening remains a gap, with traiecto and rudente still tentative.
The partly obscured paruas memini and pale transire remain tentative. No hidden initial word is supplied beneath the stain.

The visible letters immediately before talos read uix, not qui. The reading is corrected and remains qualified because of the pale ink; contigerunt remains tentative and the obscured opening remains a gap.
The surviving depositos niuibus de monte solutis is legible to the right of the opaque patch. The opening gap remains justified.
Tentative source traces retained in unclear: glaciosas. The surviving depositos niuibus de monte solutis is legible to the right of the opaque patch. The opening gap remains justified.

Only lacrimas lentus amore uidet is retained with confidence; the opening is left unreadable rather than forced into an expected construction. The surviving depositos niuibus de monte solutis is legible to the right of the opaque patch. The opening gap remains justified.
The enlarged opening remains compatible with tentative Ilia tuam, though the first group is especially faint. Aut plures inter dominabere nymphas is visible; the unusual sequence is not normalized.
Non tantum aut plures is visibly present. The line is retained as a source observation without grammatical emendation.
The name Troiana is pale but compatible with the surviving letter sequence. The qualification remains appropriate.

The opening is tentatively Cur pendit; intervening traces remain illegible. The source does not support a confident complete verse in this pass. Tentative source traces retained in unclear: Cur pendit; praecipitem. The surviving depositos niuibus de monte solutis is legible to the right of the opaque patch. The opening gap remains justified.
The apparent joined spelling Outinam is present. Editorial spacing is not used to invent a manuscript difference.
Cum poterant remains compatible with the pale centre, while uirginis ossa legi is clearer. Existing uncertainty remains local.

The V of Vestalis is visibly darker than surrounding ink. No earlier letter, mechanism of correction or historical hand is inferred. The middle and end of this line remain uncertain. Tentative source traces retained in unclear: col; dulcis. The surviving depositos niuibus de monte solutis is legible to the right of the opaque patch. The opening gap remains justified.
The enlarged central group remains compatible with tentative quam notet. The source reading is not regularized to a more familiar phrase.
Vestem remains plausible in the faint opening half. The et sign and later phrase remain visible, and the uncertainty is retained.
The possessive before tegunt is still pale and compatible with uestra. Its local uncertainty is retained.
Tuis is compatible with the small pale group before spatiosus. The image does not justify replacing it with an expected adjective.
All words are present but faint at the lower right. The complete-line unclear element remains a conservative representation of Nec capit admissas alueus altus aquas.
Image 91 left begins at this verse. The twenty final physical positions are present before the next decorated initial; the opening reading is compatible with the photograph.
Diuitas and hiemps are the apparent source spellings and remain unchanged.
The visible middle word remains compatible with mentis. No correction is made to match an expected adjective.
Uae demens remains pale and qualified. Fluminum amores is distinguishable on enlargement with letters written out, so that phrase is no longer unclear; no abbreviation sign is invented.
The enlarged sequence after quem remains compatible with tentative hunc spectas and the final amnem remains faint. Acheloon and inachon are retained as source forms.
The compact group nomenque and the pale nile referre remain tentative. The ending after nomen is not distinct enough to encode a specific abbreviation sign; no sign is fabricated.
The complete final line precedes the large initial of P 3.7. The physical sequence confirms all 106 extant positions, with illegibility distinguished from manuscript absence.

The word between totiens and uiator is less secure than the first pass implies, especially its opening letters. The existing reading adire is now qualified as unclear rather than replaced with an unsupported alternative.
